race_context: Batesville Community School Corporation (BCSC) is based in Batesville in Ripley County; its taxing area includes the City of Batesville, the town of Oldenburg and parts of Laughery, Adams, Ray, Salt Creek and Butler townships {dlgf_batesville}. State enrollment counts were 2,221 students in 2023-24, 2,220 in 2024-25 and 2,210 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}.

Superintendent: Dr. Katy Eastes, formerly assistant superintendent of New Palestine Community Schools, signed a contract in February 2026 and started that month {ec_eastes_start}{wrbi_eastes}. She followed Paul Ketcham, superintendent for nine years and the 2025 Indiana Superintendent of the Year, who left Jan. 1, 2026 to become Indiana's assistant secretary of education; former Milan superintendent Jane Rogers served as interim {wrbi_ketcham_leaving}{ec_interim}.

The board has five members {bl_candidates}. Seats are tied to residence districts; District 3, inside the City of Batesville, elected two members in 2020, and candidates must have lived in their district for at least a year {ec_2020_seats}. Ripley County's 2026 sample ballot lists the District 1, 2 and 4 races together, each 'vote for one (1) only', and notes that a straight-party vote does not count for these offices {ripley_sample}. Officers since January 2025: Stephanie Davidson (president), Blaine Timonera (vice president) and Larry Merkel (secretary); the other members are Jeremy Raver and Sean Townsley {wrbi_sworn}{wrbi_ketcham_final}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: Districts 1, 2 and 4, one seat each, which matches the state list {in_list}{ripley_sample}. Incumbents Stephanie D. Davidson (District 1) and Larry Merkel (District 2), both elected in 2022, are running unopposed. District 4 member Sean Townsley chose not to run, so the four-way District 4 race will seat a new member {bl_candidates}.

Party labels: 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party. The Batesville Leader reported that Davidson and Carla Kemper Austin chose not to disclose a party (the state list shows them as Nonpartisan), Merkel and Rob Shane filed as Republicans, Ken Baran as a Democrat and Rob Wagner as an Independent {bl_candidates}{in_list}.

Superintendent search (Oct. 2025–Feb. 2026): the board hired the University Search Team and ran a public survey, listing its priorities as continuous improvement, continuing the district's Bulldog Ready initiative, and a visible leader in the corporation, community and state {wrbi_search}. Davidson said Eastes impressed the board with 'the research she had done about our schools' {wrbi_eastes}.

Teacher pay (November 2025): BCSC and the Batesville Educators Association reached a one-year tentative agreement for 2025-26 giving most teachers a $3,100 raise and raising the district's share of health premiums by 5%; the district said it gets the lowest per-pupil funding in southeastern Indiana {wrbi_ta}.

Academics and safety: the district reported that 98.8% of third graders at Batesville Intermediate School passed IREAD in 2025, placing it in the top five among in-person public school districts in Indiana {wrbi_iread}. BCSC received an $86,000 state Secured School Safety grant in 2026 {wrbi_safety}. Starting in 2026-27, students' phones must be off and stored from the first bell to the last, in line with a new state law {ec_phone}.

Budget: the district filed its 2027 capital projects and bus replacement plans with the state in September 2026 {dlgf_batesville}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 affects BCSC's budget, and no BCSC referendum.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for these races. The only campaign statement found was a candidate-provided page from Rob Wagner on WRBI's website {wrbi_wagner}.

candidates.summary: Candidate for the open District 4 seat; a manufacturing engineer who says he would be 'an independent voice' on the board {wrbi_wagner}.
background: Says he has more than 30 years of experience as a manufacturing engineer and currently works at the Honda Indiana auto plant {wrbi_wagner}.
Lifelong Ripley County resident and Ball State University graduate; served in the U.S. Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment ('The Old Guard') {wrbi_wagner}.
Parent of two adult children who attended Batesville schools from kindergarten through 12th grade {wrbi_wagner}.
Has coached youth sports for 20 seasons, was a licensed IHSAA basketball official and is serving a third term as a cemetery board trustee {wrbi_wagner}.

items: Says he will make decisions based on 'what is best for our students, our taxpayers, and our community' and wants to make sure 'our tax dollars are spent wisely' {wrbi_wagner}.

Cites a 2010 project he helped lead on heating and cooling at a facility, which he says cut electricity and natural gas use and delayed major equipment replacement by nearly ten years, as the kind of resource planning he would bring to the board {wrbi_wagner}.
Says he is not running because he thinks he knows how to teach better than teachers or manage administrators, and that he respects education professionals {wrbi_wagner}.

on_incumbent: Says he is 'not running to change the direction of our schools or promote a personal agenda' {wrbi_wagner}.
plans: Says he would listen, study facts, ask questions and respect different viewpoints before deciding {wrbi_wagner}.
